FN-RBGS1YY-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 177
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Ben Robbins
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/18/2025
House Bill 177 as introduced could decrease the obligations of the Alabama Medicaid Agency
by an estimated maximum of $3,000 per child who would have been covered by Medicaid,
under current law, but, pursuant to this bill, who would be covered by their parent's
employer-provided health coverage.
According to the agency, approximately 50,000 children that are enrolled in Alabama's
Medicaid Program also have third-party health coverage. The annual cost of medical expenses
as payor of last resort for these children is approximately $45 million annually ($12.3 million
paid from state funds and $32.7 million in federal funds).
Further, this bill would allow the agency to recover, through civil judgment or income tax
garnishment, any amounts paid by Medicaid for medical care of children that are eligible to be
on their parent's employer-provided health coverage.

FN-RBGS1YY-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 177
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Ben Robbins
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/05/2025
House Bill 177 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary could decrease the obligations of the
Alabama Medicaid Agency by an estimated maximum of $3,000 per child who would have been
covered by Medicaid, under current law, but, pursuant to this bill, who would be covered,
pursuant to a court order, by their non-custodial parent's private health insurance .
According to the agency, approximately 50,000 children that are enrolled in Alabama's
Medicaid Program also have third-party health coverage. The annual cost of medical expenses
as payor of last resort for these children is approximately $45 million annually ($12.3 million
paid from state funds and $32.7 million in federal funds).
Further, this bill would allow the agency to recover, through civil judgment or income tax
garnishment, any amounts paid by Medicaid for medical care of children that are eligible to be
on their non-custodial parent's private health insurance pursuant to a court order, as permissible
by state or federal law.
